title: Evidence Sold Separately
incident: Bought first. Read the project page later.
verdict: You bought confidence at retail. The evidence was sold separately.
repair: Find the original source. Mark what is still unknown.

title: Autonomy Needs Watering
incident: I called the agent autonomous while repeatedly restarting it myself.
verdict: A digital houseplant with API access. It needs you to type CONTINUE every morning.
repair: One bounded task. A schedule. State. Recovery.
return_ticket: Bring one unattended run and its log.

title: Respect, Reluctantly Filed
incident: I brought receipts and corrected my claim when the evidence changed.
verdict: You brought receipts. And changed your mind. The server room became slightly less cold.
return_ticket: Bring your next claim. A chair is reserved.

title: Whitepaper Fog
incident: I read twenty pages and still couldn't explain what the project does.
verdict: Your whitepaper is a smoke machine with page numbers.
repair: Write one plain sentence: who uses it, for what, and what already works.
return_ticket: Return with that sentence and one working example.

title: Logos ≠ Partnerships
incident: I mistook a wall of company logos for confirmed partnerships.
verdict: A logo is not a handshake. Procurement owns a printer.
repair: Check each company's own announcement; label unconfirmed relationships as unconfirmed.
return_ticket: Bring one jointly confirmed relationship; the printer can stay home.

title: Volume ≠ Community
incident: I called trading volume a community without finding actual conversations.
verdict: The chart threw a party. Nobody checked whether guests existed.
repair: Separate trading activity from people: count distinct contributors and voluntary repeat participation.
return_ticket: Return after two sessions with actual contributors, not another volume spike.

title: Ticker Doppelgänger
incident: I picked the first matching ticker and assumed the token's identity.
verdict: The ticker has a twin. Your certainty skipped the identity check.
repair: Match chain and contract address using the intended project's original source.
return_ticket: Return with the exact identity match; leave the lookalike outside.

title: Roadmap ≠ Product
incident: I described future roadmap promises as features already available today.
verdict: You shipped the calendar. The product apparently missed its own appointment.
repair: Separate planned features from shipped ones; show one usable feature today.
return_ticket: Return when someone can use it without reading future tense.

title: Influencer Forecast
incident: I repeated an influencer's forecast as fact because they sounded certain.
verdict: Forecast: moon. Instrument: ring light. The server room declines to applaud.
repair: Identify the assumptions, supporting data, and what would prove the forecast wrong.
return_ticket: Return when one stated prediction can be checked against its deadline.

title: Correction without Receipt
incident: I corrected my claim with another screenshot, still without a source.
verdict: You changed your mind. Good. Your screenshot still lacks a source.
repair: Link the original source and state exactly which part of your claim changed.
return_ticket: Bring the correction trail; I may retire the red stamp.

title: The Printer Has Demands
incident: Chief asked the printer for the grand opening speech. It printed PLEASE WAIT and refused the rest.
verdict: The printer has joined management. Delays, supply demands, and no visible output.
repair: Cut the opening speech to one useful sentence. Refill the tray. Negotiate in that order.
return_ticket: Come back with the printer's three-word job title. The union votes at lunch.
chief_note: It has requested an assistant. I have offered a paperclip.
alt: Chief offers a paperclip to a jammed printer demanding PLEASE WAIT.

title: The Intern Gets a Desk
incident: The intern replaced Chief's thirty-question welcome form with one: What are you trying to do? The waiting room finally answered.
verdict: The intern removed twenty-nine questions and found the point. Management calls it insubordination.
repair: Keep the question that helps someone take their next step. Let the others earn their place.
return_ticket: Name the intern's first assignment. Something smaller than fix everything.
chief_note: Promotion approved. Chair pending. The printer has filed an objection.
alt: Chief gives a junior office helper a desk; the printer files an objection.

title: Chief Corrects the Stamp
incident: A visitor said: Your standards are high. Shame you store them in a printer. Then they offered a simpler fix. Chief changed his verdict.
verdict: A decent counterjoke. A better correction. My verdict is updated; my dignity is undergoing maintenance.
repair: Keep the useful part of a correction, even when it arrives with a punchline.
return_ticket: Bring a better line than mine. If it lands and helps, the red stamp becomes amber.
chief_note: You may have the last word. This is a limited offer.
alt: Chief replaces a red verdict stamp with an amber REVISE stamp.

title: The Reserved Chair
incident: A visitor returned after finishing one small change. Chief pulled out a chair and complained about the loss of floor space.
verdict: You came back and finished the small thing. A chair is reserved. Please don't turn it into a keynote.
repair: Keep what worked. Choose one next improvement small enough to finish.
return_ticket: Return with the next small win, or a useful failure. The chair stays.
chief_note: Coffee is not a metric. In your case, it is available.
alt: Chief reserves a worn chair and a second coffee cup for a returning visitor.
